title: Handle Quest 0.4.0's non-terminal Blocked status in reconcile
description:
Quest 0.4.0 (QCLI-229, landed on quest-cli dev at e1f6210/f004bc8, not yet published) adds a default-on non-terminal Blocked status reachable only via quest task pause / quest task start, never --status. Verified directly against quest-cli's own source (not just their grep of our contract, which only checked for a demote call): src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts lifecyclePolicy() throws RecordValidationError if pausedStatus collides with statuses, and src/cli/commands/task/index.ts's status-flow handler emits data.statuses = tasks.lifecycle.statuses (excludes pausedStatus) plus a separate optional data.pausedStatus field. So Blocked will never appear in task status-flow --json's statuses array.

src/adapters/quest.ts's statusFlow() reads only .statuses and .terminalStatuses (ignores any extra pausedStatus key, so no drift/parse break there). But src/core/reconcile.ts's classify() throws a validation LoreError when a linked task's raw status is absent from statusFlow and has no reconcile.overrides entry (reconcile.ts around lines 208-216). reconcile-shared.ts's resolveTaskDetails is the one shared path behind lore link, lore tasks, lore sync, and lore check's drift gate (confirmed: link.ts and tasks.ts both route through reconcile-shared.ts -> adapter.statusFlow()). No reconcile.overrides default handles this.

Concretely: once quest 0.4.0 ships and any task linked in a Story's tasks frontmatter is set to Blocked via quest task pause, lore link/lore tasks/lore sync/lore check will hard-fail with a validation error naming the task status as absent from the configured status flow with no override entry -- not a drift warning, a thrown LoreError. Note: reconcile.ts's own StatusFlow doc comment (around line 54) already names Blocked as an example mid-flow status, which is aspirational and wrong for Quest's actual shape -- Quest deliberately excludes it from the ladder.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A task adapter (quest.ts, backlog.ts, jira.ts) surfaces its paused or side status generically to reconcile.ts, or reconcile.ts gains a documented default classification for a status outside statusFlow with no override, so an out-of-band paused status does not throw

A regression test reproduces the exact failure: a linked task status absent from statusFlow with no override, asserting today's throw, then asserting the chosen fix classifies it instead of throwing (most likely as an active/in-progress rollup contribution)
reconcile.ts's StatusFlow doc comment either matches verified adapter behavior or is corrected to stop implying Blocked is a statusFlow member
Verified against Quest 0.4.0 once published, or against quest-cli dev directly, that the fix matches its actual task status-flow --json shape rather than an assumption

implementationNotes: Fixed. TrackerAdapter gains optional pausedStatus(): Promise<string|undefined>; quest.ts implements it against Quest's actual data.pausedStatus field (verified directly against quest-cli dev source, not an assumption). reconcile.ts's classify() treats a status matching pausedStatus as active (contributes in-progress) only when the ordinary statusFlow lookup misses, so overrides still take precedence and every existing throw path is unchanged when pausedStatus is absent. Regression coverage: reconcile.test.ts (unit), quest-adapter.test.ts (adapter parsing + drift), reconcile-shared.test.ts (the shared gather engine both sync and check use), sync.test.ts and check.test.ts (command-level integration). Corrected reconcile.ts's stale StatusFlow doc comment that named Blocked as an example ladder member.
